newsitem.title: UK: Royal Bank drops in weak bank sector.
newsitem.headline: Royal Bank drops in weak bank sector.

text.p: Shares in Royal Bank of Scotland Plc were among the biggest decliners in the FTSE 100 index on Monday, leading the bank sector lower amid continued negative sentiment towards the stock, dealers and analysts said.

Analysts said the bank may have lost out as some larger banks were bolstered by fund managers seeking to increase their weightings in the sector ahead of the imminent flotation of a number of large mutually-owned building societies.

"The sector as a whole is pretty weak and the stock is just unloved," said one analyst, who asked not to be named. "With the imminent arrival of the former building societies perhaps people are prefer to play their weightings in the bigger stocks."
Royal Bank shares were down 17p or 3.2 percent at 513 by 1418 GMT, near its four-month low of 507p set on April 1, in volume of just over one million shares.
The stock has come under sustained pressure since setting a record 636p on February 21.

Johnny de la Hay, analyst at Credit Lyonnais Laing, said he saw the recent weakness in Royal Bank shares as a buying opportunity, pointing out it had gone from the highest rated bank stocks three years ago to among the lowest.

"It is a fantastic opportunity," the Laing analyst said. "Results coming up next month are likely to be good and the sector as a whole will continue its upward move regardless of what happens on Wall Street."
De la Hay added that the Royal Bank was likely to remain a more attractive bid target than demutualising building societes such Alliance & Leicester ALL.CN and Woolwich.
